reading: The key reaches 30 models. Six were tried on the loop's first prompt. nemotron-3.5-lightning gave a version that ran in 4.9 s (193 tokens a second) and was picked. minimax-m3.1-flash took 58.6 s. The largest model, nemotron-3-ultra, took 29.9 s and its code was refused (a name starting with an underscore), as was a fourth model's; two names were not chat models.

The loop: 100 steps, 217 calls of the 300 allowed, 133,168 tokens written, 29 minutes. The model answered in a median of 0.86 s. 39 % of the time was the model; 61 % was everything else, about 9 s for each version scored. An instant model would shorten this run by at most 39 %.

Of the model's 118 versions 53 ran and 65 did not. 38 of the 65 changed what the function takes; the others were not Python, used a name the checker refuses, or did not define the function. 12 were repaired on a second or third try.

The champion proposes the law itself on 1 of the 40 training laws (the seed: 0), on none of the 40 validation laws (the seed: 0), and on none of 60 laws drawn afterwards (the seed: 0). No gain in laws proposed.
It does return an accurate candidate, which is not the law, on more of the 60 fresh laws: 15 against 6 (13 gained, 4 lost; could be chance, p = 0.049). On the validation laws: 10 against 7.

So the loop runs end to end with a real model at a cost of minutes, and what it improved is the part of the score it could move, accurate candidates. It did not find laws. One model, one run, one grammar.
not_shown: that a champion helps the route. That needs the champion beside the searches, through the referee, on laws from elsewhere; it was not run.
